topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: Answer these questions about famous American criminals.
question.text: This criminal was able to break out of what was said to be an "escape-proof" jail in 1934. He and his namesake gang terrorized the Midwest, allegedly robbing 24 banks and four police stations.
question.clue: A raid on this man at the Little Bohemia Lodge in Wisconsin turned into a full-on gunfight, during which Helen Gillis, the wife of his associate "Baby Face" Nelson, was captured.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the political career of Franklin D. Roosevelt.
swap.text: In 1932, FDR defeated this man to become president. This president's administration oversaw the beginning of the Great Depression, for which he was widely unpopular.
swap.clue: Near the end of his term, he sent Douglas MacArthur to clear out the Bonus Army that was protesting for relief from the Great Depression.

question.leadin: Name some organizations established during the New Deal.
question.text: This largest New Deal agency was created by the Emergency Relief Appropriation Act of 1935 and provided jobs and income to the unemployed; it also operated large arts, media, and literacy projects.
question.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

swap.text: This 31 st president was largely blamed for the Great Depression, and disgruntled citizens set up makeshift shantytowns sarcastically nicknamed after him.
swap.clue: This man supervised the response to the Great Mississippi Flood.

question.leadin: This man participated in a campaign where he avidly destroyed pinball machines with sledgehammers.
question.text: Name this Italian-American mayor who was dubbed "the Little Flower." He co-sponsored an act with Senator George Norris which banned yellow-dog contracts.
question.answerHtml: Fiorello La Guardia [or Fiorello Henry La Guardia; or Fiorello Raffaele Enrico La Guardia]
question.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

swap.leadin: This group camped on Anacostia Flats and was led by Walter Waters.
swap.text: Name this group of angry World War I veterans who, in 1932, demanded early payments of their pension.
swap.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

question.leadin: -answer the following about history you might encounter while hiking the Appalachian Trail.
question.text: Right before entering Virginia, you pass over Watauga Dam, one of the many dams built by this New Deal agency. Appalachian Trail founder Benton MacKaye worked for this agency after leaving the Forest Service.
question.clue: The Muscle Shoals Bill, vetoed by Herbert Hoover, was the initial impetus for this organization.

swap.text: This 1930s environmental disaster caused a mass migration of workers away from states like Oklahoma. It disproved the "rain follows the plow" superstition and contributed to the Great Depression.
swap.clue: This event saw numerous storms referred to as black blizzards.

question.leadin: This woman sent a letter to the New York Times complaining about being called "Mrs. Putnam" rather than her birth name.
question.text: Name this woman who celebrated other women pioneers in her field in her memoir The Fun of It. This woman died en route to Howland Island.
question.clue: One theory surrounding the whereabouts of this person and their companion, Fred Noonan, was that they were executed by Japanese soldiers on Saipan.

swap.text: It is entitled to borrow up to three billion dollars from the U.S. treasury. Managed by two presidentially appointed directors and the Comptroller of the Currency, it was established in 1933 to prevent a repeat of the bank collapse. For 15 points, name this federal corporation which insures up to 100,000 dollars in bank accounts.
swap.clue: This government agency established to bail out financial institutions in the event of a run on banks, which insures accounts up to one hundred thousand dollars.

question.leadin: This politician campaigned for governor with the slogan "Every man a king, but no one wears a crown."
question.text: Name this Louisiana politician, nicknamed "The Kingfish," who proposed the "Share Our Wealth" program as a senator. This politician was assassinated by Carl Weiss just prior to a likely run in the 1936 presidential election.
question.clue: This figure allied with the preacher Gerald Smith to promote an idea which he explained in a speech about God's invitation to a feast and explained that idea further in his posthumously published autobiography, My First Days in the White House.

swap.text: This 1930 tariff, which raised duties on over 20, 000 goods, is regarded by many historians as a major factor in the deepening of the Great Depression.
swap.clue: Franklin Delano Roosevelt signed the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934 as a direct Democratic response to this Republican legislation.

question.leadin: Answer the following concerning the illustrious career of Brown graduate Charles Evan Hughes.
question.text: As Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, Hughes wrote the majority opinion in this 1935 case, which ruled that the National Industrial Recovery Act's regulations of a poultry corporation were unconstitutional.
question.answer: Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States
question.clue: This 1935 Supreme Court Case that ruled a certain piece of New Deal legislation had overreached itself because the namesake company did not engage in direct interstate commerce.

swap.leadin: Journalist Dainis Ivans ("dye-niss EE-vons") rose to popularity, and eventually became the first leader of Tautas Fronte, after successfully opposing a proposed structure of this type.
swap.text: Name these structures. The illicit trade of caviar in Russia increased when sturgeon populations decreased after the building of one of these structures on the Volga River.
swap.clue: Argentina briefly opposed the building of one of these structures, named Itaipu, between Paraguay and Brazil on the Paran´a River.

question.text: In a speech, Perkins described this man responding only "Okay" to her proposal of unemployment insurance. Perkins and this head of the PWA were the only cabinet members to remain in office for FDR's entire presidency.
question.answerHtml: Harold L. Ickes (“ICK-iss”) [do not accept or prompt on “Harold M. Ickes”]
question.clue: One person with this last name chaired Bill Clinton's 1992 presidential campaign and was nicknamed the "Garbage Man" by (+) Michael Lewis in an unflattering 1997 profile.

swap.text: Amended by the Landrum-Griffin act, this New Deal legislation created the National Labor Relations Board and allowed for collective bargaining, catalyzing the growth of labor unions.
swap.clue: Chief Justice Charles Hughes wrote the majority opinion in the resulting Supreme Court case against the Jones and Laughlin steel company that upheld the application of this law to interstate commerce.

question.leadin: While its first chairman was Peter Norbeck, this group was named for its fourth chief counsel, who would later become a commissioner of the SEC.
question.text: Name this commission which was established to explore the causes of the Wall Street Crash of 1929.
question.clue: Among the sections in the 400-page report produced by this investigative body were ones on "Manipulative devices," and "Abuse of proxies," as well as a chapter dedicated to investigating "Income-tax Avoidances."

swap.leadin: John Hart Ely's Democracy and Distrust builds on Justice Harlan Stone's opinion in this case by arguing that the Warren Court's activism was not values-based but process-based.
swap.text: Name this Supreme Court case, whose Footnote Four introduced the basis for strict scrutiny by proposing a "narrower scope for operation of the presumption of constitutionality."
swap.clue: This 1938 Supreme Court case, which is more famous for its "footnote four."

question.text: This man was the first director of the NRA and Time's Man of the Year in 1933. He called for a "blanket code" including a minimum wage, maximum workweek, and abolition of child labor, but was fired in 1934 after handing out leaflets praising Mussolini's "Corporate State."

swap.leadin: Tom McCoy was a principal actor in this event, which in the span of a single day used the favorable results of a recount to reorganize the entire government of Rhode Island.
swap.text: Identify this pivotal event of Rhode Island history which took place on January 1, 1935, and in which a possible case of voter fraud allowed Democrats to assume complete control of state politics.
